source.title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
source.summary: Modern LLM coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenHands share a common inefficiency: they spend much of their token budget finding the file to patch, rather than patching it. On SWE-Bench Verified, a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, with many calls spent on grep, glob, and view_file during repository exploration. We introduce CodeGrep, a 14B retrieval agent trained end-to-end with GRPO to issue multi-turn parallel grep, glob, and read tool calls and return candidate files to a frozen downstream coding agent. On all 500 SWE-Bench Verified instances, CodeGrep preserves resolve rate while substantially improving efficiency: 27.0% versus 25.8% for the no-retrieval baseline, with 15% fewer rounds and 19% fewer tokens on resolved instances. Across retrievers, downstream utility follows a precision threshold: BM25 with precision 0.375 degrades the agent, Jina with precision 0.445 is neutral, and CodeGrep with precision 0.677 crosses the threshold at which retrieval begins to reduce rollout cost. To enable this study, we mine supervision from 67K open-source agent trajectories using CATM and build a Git-worktree environment for multi-turn agent RL. In our setting, applying the efficiency signal at the advantage layer rather than the reward layer reduces KL drift and translates cleanly into downstream efficiency. We will release the model, training pipeline, RL environment, and evaluation harnesses.

previous_facts.title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
previous_facts.event_hint: CodeGrep: 14B retrieval agent trained with GRPO to reduce coding agent file exploration overhead
previous_facts.problem: Modern LLM coding agents (Claude Code, OpenHands) spend most of their token budget finding the file to patch rather than patching it. On SWE-Bench Verified, a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, with a large fraction consumed by grep, glob, and view_file calls during ambiguous exploration loops—often 20+ rounds in wrong directions before the agent gives up.
previous_facts.mechanism: CodeGrep is a 14B-parameter retrieval agent built on Qwen3-14B-Instruct, trained end-to-end with GRPO to issue multi-turn parallel grep/glob/read tool calls and return candidate files to a frozen downstream coding agent. It exposes three read-only primitives (regex search, path matching, file contents) mirroring developer navigation. At each turn it emits up to 8 tool calls executed concurrently. During inference, CodeGrep takes the issue description, emits candidate files, and those files are injected into the prompt of a frozen OpenHands downstream agent—only the retriever is trained.

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Evaluation on SWE-Bench Verified (500 instances) using OpenHands with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 as downstream agent, temperature 0, 100-round max. Baseline without retrieval resolves 25.8% at 23.0 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue. Training uses 67K open-source agent trajectories mined via CATM, with GLM-5.1-FP8 as judge model. Training on single 8xB200 node with LoRA, 27-hour wall-clock per run, early-stop at step 897 of 2000-step budget. Environment supports thousands of unique (repo,commit) pairs with 64 asyncio semaphore for tool concurrency, max 8 parallel tools per turn, 32 max tool execs per rollout.
previous_facts.limitations: Evaluation limited to SWE-Bench Verified benchmark only—no production deployment data or real-world coding workflows reported. The line-range component was removed because downstream OpenHands editor has no view_range argument, making predicted line ranges dead information at inference time. Training data includes CATM-only entries with no gold line ranges by construction, introducing systematic label bias. The downstream agent is frozen (OpenHands), so results may not generalize to other coding agents like Claude Code. Precision threshold regime characterization based on only three retrievers (BM25, Jina, CodeGrep). End-to-end wall-clock latency not reported, only token and round metrics.
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to Agent semantic acceleration focus on reducing repetitive Read, Grep, Glob, and code exploration. CodeGrep demonstrates a clear precision threshold (≈0.45-0.50) below which retrieval degrades downstream agent and above which it buys efficiency. This directly addresses current questions about whether repository indices truly reduce end-to-end task latency—CodeGrep shows 15% rounds reduction and 19% tokens reduction while preserving resolve rate. The work quantifies tool call overhead (2.3 average turns per rollout) and shows retrieval must cross precision ≈0.677 to translate into downstream efficiency. However, CodeGrep does not address repository index construction cost, false positive rates, error recovery overhead, or whether parallel tool calls introduce correctness risk—limitations that project context specifically asks for.
